I wrote the 30-minute lesson on O3, with a short quiz and a cheat sheet. I haven't run any word-count or link check on the lesson.

- **Lesson:** `lessons/0001-context-and-memory-in-an-agent.html`
  - It opens with the win: for any piece of information in the makerspace assistant, say where it lives (the context, a saved note, or a searched manual) and why.
  - It has a warm-up on the agent loop, then five sections:
    - the context window;
    - what is kept between steps (the program re-sends the whole history on every call);
    - when the context fills up (context rot, clearing old tool results, compaction);
    - notes as memory between sessions (both a save step and a load step are needed);
    - retrieval (up front versus just in time).
  - It has three figures, a check after each section, and a worked token-cost comparison (about 127k tokens for pasting a manual versus about 7k for retrieving a chunk). The numbers are illustrative.
  - Your turn is a similar calculation, then naming where each fact would live.
  - From my section plan it should be about 4,000 words, inside the 2,700–6,750 range that fits 30 minutes.
- **Primary source:** Anthropic's [Effective context engineering for AI agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents). A subagent opened it and I relied on its report.
